messages:
Sophie: Heads-up — we plan to change /v1/generate response shape next week for model variants. Short summary: removing `metadata.flags` and adding `usage.category` (string). This is a minor API change but could break light schema consumers. Need a quick compatibility check and rollout plan.

Omar: Can you confirm the exact timeline? Which customers will be impacted? Do we have a compatibility header to gate clients?

Sophie: Proposed timeline: announce today, soft-deprecate old field for 14 days (still present but will be undocumented), then cut the field at EOD 2026-03-31. Canary rollout starts Mon to 10% of hosted traffic, then ramp. Dedicated/private customers get 60-day opt-in window (config flag).

Maria: For the contract, I suggest we add `X-Redwood-API-Version: 2026-03-17` to responses for the new shape so clients can detect the response format. Also add a `compatibility` flag in the `/models` catalog: `response_shapes: ["2025-12","2026-03"]`. That helps SDKs pick parsing logic.

Ajay: SDKs will need new parsers. Two quick questions: 1) Does `model_pin` still guarantee previous output shape if you pin to a prior model? 2) Will we emit a warning header for deprecated fields?

Sophie: Good Qs. 1) Yes — pinning to an explicit model version (e.g., `model_pin: "redwood-gpt-medium@2025-11-12"`) will preserve the prior response shape and behavior. We should document that explicitly. 2) We'll emit `X-Redwood-Deprecation: metadata.flags; fri=1748716800` (timestamp for removal) and also add a `deprecation_warnings` array in the initial response for canary users.

Linh: I'll add a CI contract test that runs a small suite against both shapes. Plan: record golden responses for pinned model, validate new schema with `ajv` and also run a lightweight JSON Schema check in integration. Snippet we can add to repo: 

```
# run schema check
curl -s "${BASE_URL}/v1/generate?model=redwood-gpt-medium@2025-11-12" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" \
  | jq '. | {text: .choices[0].text, usage: .usage}' > out.json
ajv validate -s schemas/generate-2026-03.json -d out.json
```

Omar: For observability, can we log when clients receive deprecated fields? That will help surface who still relies on `metadata.flags` before we cut it.

Sophie: Yes — add a metric `deprecated_field_seen{field="metadata.flags"}` and a trace event when `X-Redwood-Deprecation` is present. Product will use that to trigger customer comms.

Ajay: Who owns the customer notification email + docs update? I can handle SDK changelog and minor release.

Maria: I'll own docs + API reference. Can we draft the deprecation note to include migration example (old -> new)? Eg: `usage.category = metadata.flags ? "interactive" : "batch"` (very rough).

Sophie: Assignments: Maria -> docs + deprecation blog; Ajay -> SDK patch + unit tests; Linh -> CI contract tests & schema; Omar -> telemetry dashboard + metric alerts; Sophie -> customer comms + canary config.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout scheduled: hosted/generate v2-response-shape -> 2026-03-22 06:00 UTC -> 10% -> monitoring window 48h.

Sophie: Thanks — I'll push the announce draft to #announcements by EOD and add the compat matrix to the models catalog. Ping me if your PR needs a quick review. :thumbsup:

Omar: LGTM, will start the dashboard.

Ajay: Will open SDK PR today and tag you for review.

Linh: I'll wire the AJV check into the matrix job and add a job to run pinned-model golden responses nightly.

Maria: Drafting docs now, will add migration snippet and add the `X-Redwood-API-Version` example.

Sophie: Great — closing this thread once PRs are linked.
